title: Constructible derived comparison for arbitrary finite rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. Use the small etale and pro-etale sites, their coefficient sheaves, and the exact derived inverse image $\nu_X^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The functor $\nu_X^*$ induces an equivalence between bounded etale complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and pro-etale complexes whose cohomology is intrinsically constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and vanishes outside a finite interval. It preserves and reflects each cohomological interval $[a,b]$. In particular every such pro-etale complex has bounded constructible etale origin. No assumption that $B$ is a quotient of a discrete valuation ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived (and exact cohomology comparison); applies to every Noetherian ring, hence every finite ring

proof.text: Put $F=\nu_X^*$. A finite ring has finitely many ideals, so ascending chains stabilize and $B$ is Noetherian. The sheaf comparison [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin] supplies preservation and reflection of constructibility and an etale origin for every intrinsically constructible sheaf. Throughout, constructibility means the global finite-stratification notions stated by the two definition nodes, not an identification of these notions with affine-local constructibility on arbitrary schemes.

By [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], $F$ is exact on module sheaves. For a representing complex, exactness preserves kernels, images and their quotients, giving $\mathcal H^i(F L)\cong F\mathcal H^i(L)$ by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], the termwise derived functor commutes with shifts and preserves distinguished triangles. The sheaf equivalence therefore sends every bounded constructible etale complex to an intrinsically constructible pro-etale complex in the same interval. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], this derived functor is fully faithful on $D^+$, hence also on the full bounded constructible subcategory.

Let $K$ have intrinsically constructible cohomology vanishing outside $[a,b]$. If all its cohomology is zero (in particular if $a>b$), a representing complex is acyclic and $0\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $K\cong0=F(0)$ in the localization defining the derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Otherwise $a\leq b$. Induct on the nonnegative integer $b-a$, with the claim that $K\cong F L$ for a bounded constructible etale $L$ in $[a,b]$. For $a=b$, [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] identifies $K\cong\mathcal H^a(K)[-a]$. Choose a constructible etale sheaf $G$ with $FG\cong\mathcal H^a(K)$ by the sheaf comparison. Then $L=G[-a]$ has the required cohomology, and the shift and single-complex compatibility of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] gives $F L\cong K$.

source.place: Tag 09AL, bounded truncation induction; derived.tex Tag 08J5 single-degree case

proof.text: For $a<b$, take the distinguished truncation triangle $K_-\to K\to K_+\xrightarrow{\delta}K_-[1]$ supplied by [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle], with $\mathcal H^n(K_-)=0$ for $n\geq b$ and $\mathcal H^n(K_+)=0$ for $n<b$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. For $n<b$, the adjacent groups $\mathcal H^{n-1}(K_+)$ and $\mathcal H^n(K_+)$ are zero, so $\mathcal H^n(K_-)\to\mathcal H^n(K)$ is an isomorphism. For $n\geq b$, the adjacent groups $\mathcal H^n(K_-)$ and $\mathcal H^{n+1}(K_-)$ are zero, so $\mathcal H^n(K)\to\mathcal H^n(K_+)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $K_-$ and $K_+$ have constructible cohomology in $[a,b-1]$ and $[b,b]$, respectively. The induction hypothesis and the base case give etale origins $L_-$ and $L_+$ with these same bounds, with chosen isomorphisms $F L_-\cong K_-$ and $F L_+\cong K_+$.

Using the chosen origins and the shift isomorphism of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], view $\delta$ as a morphism $F L_+\to F(L_-[1])$. Both source objects $L_+$ and $L_-[1]$ are bounded below. Full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] therefore lifts it uniquely to $d:L_+\to L_-[1]$. Apply TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $-d[-1]:L_+[-1]\to L_-$, obtaining a distinguished triangle $L_+[-1]\xrightarrow{-d[-1]}L_-\to H\to L_+$. Its rotation by TR2 is $L_-\to H\to L_+\xrightarrow{d}L_-[1]$, since the new last arrow is $-(-d[-1])[1]=d$. Its image under $F$ is distinguished by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Transport its outer terms along the chosen isomorphisms and rotate twice; both it and the twice-rotated truncation triangle now begin with $K_+\xrightarrow{\delta}K_-[1]$. TR3, applied to the identity on these first two terms, produces a morphism of distinguished triangles. These two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third component $F H[1]\to K[1]$ an isomorphism. Inverse shift gives $F H\cong K$.

The constructed etale object $H$ is bounded constructible in $[a,b]$. Indeed Step 2 gives $F\mathcal H^i(H)\cong\mathcal H^i(K)$. If $i$ is outside $[a,b]$, apply $
u_{X,*}$ to this isomorphism and use the underived unit $\mathcal H^i(H)\cong
u_{X,*}F\mathcal H^i(H)$ from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] to conclude $\mathcal H^i(H)=0$. Within the interval, the sheaf equivalence gives a constructible etale $G_i$ with $F G_i\cong\mathcal H^i(K)$. The unit makes $F$ fully faithful on all sheaves: its adjunction identifies maps $F A	o F B$ with maps $A	o
u_{X,*}FB\cong B$. Thus $F\mathcal H^i(H)\cong F G_i$ implies $\mathcal H^i(H)\cong G_i$, proving constructibility. This closes the induction and supplies essential surjectivity.

For any etale complex $L$, Step 2 gives $\mathcal H^i(F L)\cong F\mathcal H^i(L)$. Vanishing of $\mathcal H^i(L)$ implies vanishing of its image; conversely vanishing of its image implies vanishing of $\mathcal H^i(L)$ by the underived unit of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. Hence the property of vanishing outside each interval $[a,b]$ is both preserved and reflected (including the empty-interval zero case). Together with full faithfulness and the induction this proves the stated equivalence and the bounded constructible etale-origin conclusion.
